Chapter Details: The architecture, governance, functionality and uptake of government digital payment systems.  21 variables in 4 sections. Contains latest available data. Data collection by Perplexity from a variety of sources.
Definition: Whether the scheme rules governing payment system participation, pricing structure, technical requirements, security standards, and conduct are publicly accessible via website, public repository, or on request. Transparency indicator.
Comments: Value=3 (yes, fully public): BCEAO publishes public pages describing operating rules and procedures for STAR-UEMOA (e.g., finality, priority processing, settlement-account checks) and SICA-UEMOA includes detailed operating procedures and participation requirements, indicating scheme rules are publicly accessible online ([BCEAO STAR-UEMOA](https://www.bceao.int/en/content/star-uemoa);[BCEAO SICA-UEMOA](https://www.bceao.int/en/content/sica-uemoa)).

Chapter Details: The architecture, governance, functionality and uptake of government digital payment systems.  21 variables in 4 sections. Contains latest available data. Data collection by Perplexity from a variety of sources.
Definition: Whether the country has established or is actively developing an instant/real-time payment system (IPS/RTP) that enables digital payments with near-instant settlement (typically within seconds), available 24/7/365. This includes both bank-led and mobile money interoperability systems.
Comments: Value=4 (partially deployed): Niger is in WAEMU/UEMOA where BCEAO operates regional retail clearing (SICA-UEMOA) and RTGS (STAR-UEMOA) systems used by banks and national treasuries in all member states, providing interbank electronic payment infrastructure rather than a Niger-only instant retail system ([BCEAO payment systems management](https://www.bceao.int/en/content/payment-systems-management);[BCEAO STAR-UEMOA](https://www.bceao.int/en/content/star-uemoa)).

Chapter Details: The architecture, governance, functionality and uptake of government digital payment systems.  21 variables in 4 sections. Contains latest available data. Data collection by Perplexity from a variety of sources.
Definition: Percentage of the adult population (15+ years) who have made at least one digital payment transaction through the instant payment system in the past 90 days, indicating active usage rather than just account ownership.
Comments: Value=1 (<20%): One available Niger-focused payments overview notes that only about 9% of people in Niger use mobile money, indicating low active digital payment usage (<20%) ([Transfi – Niger’s Payment Rails](https://www.transfi.com/blog/nigers-payment-rails-how-they-work---gim-uemoa-mobile-money-cross-border-payment-links)).
